question.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}-5{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-5{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(1-5y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}y({y}^{2}-5{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}({y}^{3}-5{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1/5}-5\cdot {\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1/5}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4\cdot {5}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{5}^{5}}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{{5}^{4}}(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{20\cdot {5}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6\,250}\end{aligned}
$$
